name: Melanotan II
summary: Synthetic melanocortin agonist that darkens skin by cranking melanin production. Also hits arousal and appetite.
lead: Melanotan II (MT-II) is a synthetic cyclic peptide analogue of the hormone alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH). It stimulates melanin production and was originally developed as a sunless tanning agent; it also increases sexual arousal in some users . It acts as a non-selective agonist at several melanocortin receptors, which is why its effects extend beyond skin pigmentation to appetite and erections .
claims: It produces a deep, lasting tan with minimal UV exposure
It is a safe way to protect skin from sunburn
It boosts libido and causes spontaneous erections
Gray-market melanotan is the same as prescription afamelanotide

name: Afamelanotide
summary: MC1R agonist that boosts eumelanin and photoprotection.
lead: Afamelanotide, sold as Scenesse and originally called melanotan I, is a synthetic analogue of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH) that is delivered as a subcutaneous implant. It is approved to reduce phototoxicity in adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), a rare inherited condition in which light exposure causes severe pain .
claims: Melanotan 1 is safer than melanotan 2
MT1 causes fewer moles than MT2
MT1 darkens freckles
Melanotan can reduce UV damage over time

name: Dihydroxyacetone
summary: The active in every self-tanner: stains the outer skin layer brown. The only proven-safe tan in a bottle.
lead: Dihydroxyacetone (DHA, also called glycerone) is a three-carbon sugar and the active ingredient in most sunless tanning lotions, sprays, mousses, wipes and salon spray tans . It darkens the outermost layer of the skin through a Maillard reaction with amino acids in keratin, producing brown pigments called melanoidins; the colour is a surface stain rather than new melanin .
claims: Self-tanner is a safe alternative to UV tanning
Self-tanner gives sun protection
Streaks and blotches can be removed by scrubbing
Face application needs care around eyes, mouth and hairline

name: Canthaxanthin
summary: Carotenoid "tanning pill" that tints skin orange-brown at high doses.
lead: Canthaxanthin is an orange-red keto-carotenoid pigment (C40H52O2) found in some mushrooms, algae, bacteria and crustaceans, and used as a food and feed colourant, for example to colour farmed salmon, trout and egg yolks . When swallowed in large amounts, it deposits in fat beneath the skin and gives a golden-orange tint, which is why it was sold in oral 'tanning pills' .
claims: Canthaxanthin pills give a tan
It is natural and therefore safe
It is legal over the counter
The same pigment colours farmed salmon

name: Beta-carotene
summary: Gives skin a warmer, golden tone with sustained daily intake.
lead: Beta-carotene is a yellow-orange carotenoid pigment found in carrots, sweet potatoes and leafy greens, and is a dietary precursor of vitamin A . It is sold as a supplement and is discussed in looksmaxxing communities as a way to give skin a warmer, golden tone through sustained oral intake .
claims: Beta-carotene pills give a natural-looking golden tan
Beta-carotene does nothing
Lycopene and astaxanthin are better than beta-carotene for tan or glow
Excess beta-carotene produces an orange look that is unattractive

name: Lycopene
summary: Tomato carotenoid with antioxidant and mild photoprotective effects.
lead: Lycopene is a bright red carotenoid hydrocarbon found in tomatoes, watermelon, pink grapefruit, red guava and some other red fruits and vegetables. Unlike beta-carotene, it has no vitamin A activity, and it is also used as a food colour (E160d) . It is taken through food, especially cooked tomato products eaten with fat, and as a supplement .
claims: Lycopene supports prostate health
Lycopene helps lower blood pressure
Lycopene protects skin from sun damage

name: Astaxanthin
summary: Carotenoid studied for UV damage, skin moisture, and elasticity.
lead: Astaxanthin is a red keto-carotenoid pigment produced by the freshwater microalga Haematococcus pluvialis, the yeast Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous and the bacterium Paracoccus carotinifaciens, and it is responsible for the pink-red colour of salmon, shrimp, krill and flamingos . It is sold as a dietary supplement and, in synthetic form, is widely used as a feed colourant in aquaculture .
claims: Astaxanthin is a powerful anti-inflammatory
It improves skin moisture and elasticity
It protects against UV skin damage
It helps control oestrogen on TRT

name: Polypodium leucotomos
summary: Fern extract that blunts some UV-induced skin reactions.
lead: Polypodium leucotomos is the older botanical name for Phlebodium aureum, an epiphytic fern native to tropical and subtropical regions of the Americas. Extract from its leaves is sold as an oral supplement, including under the Heliocare name, and has been studied in dermatology as an 'internal' or systemic photoprotective agent .
claims: It works as an 'internal sunscreen'
It helps melasma and pigmentation
It improves vitiligo repigmentation with phototherapy

name: Glutathione
summary: Antioxidant heavily marketed for skin lightening; visible results are inconsistent.
lead: Glutathione (GSH) is a tripeptide built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine. It is the most abundant low-molecular-weight thiol in most cell types and acts as an antioxidant, protecting cellular components from reactive oxygen species, peroxides and heavy metals, and it takes part in the detoxification of drugs and other xenobiotics .
claims: Glutathione can lighten skin tone
Injectable glutathione is the 'real deal' and works better than pills
Oral glutathione is destroyed in the gut and does nothing
Glutathione works as a general detox and health booster for lifters

name: L-Cysteine
summary: Antioxidant precursor tied to melanin pathways; weak lightening evidence.
lead: Cysteine is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid whose side chain carries a thiol (sulfhydryl) group. The L-form is a building block of proteins in all organisms; the thiol lets cysteine residues form disulfide bonds that stabilize protein structure, as in keratin, and bind metal ions . Humans can usually make it from methionine through the transsulfuration pathway, and it is also supplied by foods such as poultry, eggs, beef and whole grains .
claims: L-cysteine supports hair growth
Cysteine (or NAC) helps restore SHBG or hormone markers after steroid use
Cysteine raises glutathione, so it protects the liver and body
Cysteine availability lightens skin by steering melanin toward pheomelanin

name: Tretinoin
summary: The gold-standard retinoid: builds collagen, smooths fine wrinkles, clears acne, reverses photoaging.
lead: Tretinoin is all-trans retinoic acid, the biologically active acid form of vitamin A. Applied to the skin as a prescription cream, gel or lotion (brand names include Retin-A), it is used for acne and for photoaged skin, where it is used to smooth fine wrinkles, roughness and uneven pigmentation. Taken by mouth in capsules, the same molecule is a cancer drug used to induce remission in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) .
claims: Tretinoin is the gold-standard anti-aging ingredient and beats retinol
Tretinoin clears acne
Early purging and irritation are signs it is working and should be pushed through
Tretinoin can make skin worse or cause systemic symptoms in some people

name: Retinol
summary: OTC vitamin-A derivative; converts to retinoic acid in skin.
lead: Retinol is the alcohol form of vitamin A (vitamin A1), a fat-soluble vitamin found in fish, dairy and meat and needed for vision, cell differentiation, skin and mucous-membrane maintenance, immune function and reproductive development. It is used as a supplement to treat and prevent vitamin A deficiency and, applied to the skin, as one of the most common over-the-counter anti-aging cosmetic ingredients .
claims: Retinol under the eyes can fill out thin, dark-circled skin
Starting retinol gives clearer, 'glass skin' results and helps acne scars and eye circles
Retinol is a gentler alternative to tretinoin

name: Adapalene
summary: OTC retinoid for acne and texture — the strongest retinoid you can buy without a script.
lead: Adapalene, sold under the brand name Differin among others, is a third-generation synthetic topical retinoid used mainly for mild to moderate acne vulgaris. It is used off-label for keratosis pilaris and has been explored for photoaging and other conditions . Since 2016 a 0.1 percent adapalene gel has been available over the counter in the United States, the first formerly prescription-only retinoid to be sold that way for acne .
claims: Adapalene gel is more effective than tretinoin
Adapalene is a reasonable first option for closed comedones and mild acne when tretinoin is hard to obtain
Differin gel clears acne on the face, back and shoulders, including acne during testosterone use

name: Tazarotene
summary: Potent topical retinoid for acne and photoaging.
lead: Tazarotene, sold as Tazorac, Arazlo and other brands, is a third-generation acetylenic topical retinoid used for acne vulgaris and plaque psoriasis. Certain formulations are also used to reduce signs of photoaging such as fine facial wrinkles and mottled pigmentation. It is a prodrug converted in the skin to the active tazarotenic acid . It was approved for medical use in 1997 and is available as a generic .
claims: Tazarotene works faster than tretinoin for anti-aging and acne
Tazarotene is far more aggressive than tretinoin, causing heavy peeling and sun sensitivity
Retinoids such as tretinoin change skin to resemble female skin or give a particular 'glow'

name: Isotretinoin
summary: Systemic retinoid for severe, treatment-resistant acne.
lead: Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid), sold under the brand name Accutane and others, is an oral retinoid related to vitamin A. It is approved for severe recalcitrant nodular acne, and dermatologists also use it for moderate acne that resists other treatment or causes scarring or psychological distress, as well as for conditions such as harlequin ichthyosis . The US label reserves it for severe nodular acne unresponsive to conventional therapy including systemic antibiotics .
claims: Isotretinoin is the decisive fix for stubborn acne
Isotretinoin can cause lasting hormonal or libido problems requiring PCT-style recovery
Isotretinoin causes depression
Isotretinoin is safe to combine with anabolic steroids or heavy training

name: Botulinum toxin A
summary: Relaxes facial muscles to erase dynamic wrinkles.
lead: Botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) is a neurotoxic protein made by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum. It blocks release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction, causing temporary flaccid paralysis of the injected muscle. In heavily diluted form it is used for medical and cosmetic purposes, and commercial products include Botox Cosmetic, Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau and Daxxify .
claims: Botox leaves faces frozen and unable to express emotion
Botox smooths dynamic wrinkles in the upper face
Botulinum toxin can slim the jaw or treat clenching

name: Azelaic acid
summary: Triple threat: acne, redness, and dark spots in one ingredient.
lead: Azelaic acid (nonanedioic acid) is a nine-carbon saturated dicarboxylic acid found naturally in grains such as wheat, rye and barley and produced on human skin by the yeast Malassezia furfur. Industrially it is made by ozonolysis of oleic acid and is used in polymers, plasticizers and lubricants, as well as in some hair and skin conditioners.
claims: Azelaic acid is a 'DHT inhibitor' that helps hair loss when applied to the scalp
Minoxidil plus azelaic acid scalp mixtures improve hair retention
Azelaic acid treats acne, redness and dark spots with one product
Azelaic acid is a safe alternative to hydroquinone for melasma

name: Niacinamide
summary: Barrier support, oil control, and pigment evening.
lead: Niacinamide, also called nicotinamide, is the amide form of vitamin B3. It is found in foods such as yeast, meat, milk and green vegetables, is sold as a dietary supplement and medication, and is incorporated into cosmetic serums, moisturizers and cleansers. Within cells it is a precursor of the coenzymes NAD+ and NADP+, which take part in many oxidation-reduction reactions. Unlike nicotinic acid (niacin), it does not cause skin flushing at ordinary doses.
claims: Niacinamide improves anxiety and stress resilience
Niacinamide supports energy and brain function through NAD+
Niacinamide helps with hormone or TRT-related symptoms
Niacinamide lowers cholesterol like niacin

name: Vitamin C (topical)
summary: Antioxidant that brightens, fades spots, and supports collagen pathways.
lead: Topical vitamin C refers to skin-care products containing L-ascorbic acid or one of its derivatives, applied to the skin rather than taken by mouth. Vitamin C is a water-soluble vitamin that humans must obtain from diet; it serves as a cofactor in collagen formation and acts as an antioxidant. In cosmetic and dermatological use it is promoted for brightening, fading dark spots and reducing signs of photoaging.
claims: Fat-soluble vitamin C esters work better on skin than ascorbic acid
Topical vitamin C fades dark spots and melasma
Topical vitamin C reverses photoaging and wrinkles
Vitamin C helps stretch marks and adrenal recovery

name: Tranexamic acid
summary: Melasma and stubborn hyperpigmentation fighter, topical or oral (oral = Rx).
lead: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a synthetic derivative of the amino acid lysine that acts as an antifibrinolytic: it reversibly binds lysine-binding sites on plasminogen, reducing conversion to plasmin and so slowing the breakdown of fibrin clots. It is used to prevent or treat bleeding in trauma, postpartum haemorrhage, surgery, tooth removal, nosebleeds and heavy menstrual bleeding, and it is on the WHO List of Essential Medicines.
claims: Oral tranexamic acid clears stubborn melasma
Topical TXA is as good as hydroquinone with fewer drawbacks
Tranexamic acid is just a cosmetic ingredient

name: Hydroquinone
summary: The strongest proven pigment suppressor for dark spots.
lead: Hydroquinone (benzene-1,4-diol) is an aromatic compound and a phenol. Industrially it is best known as a photographic developing agent and polymerization inhibitor; in dermatology it is applied topically as a skin-lightening agent for melasma, solar lentigines (sun spots) and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, alone or in combination creams. The name was coined by Friedrich Wohler in 1843.
claims: Hydroquinone is the strongest dark-spot treatment
Hydroquinone is dangerous and carcinogenic
Long-term or high-strength use can darken the skin permanently

name: Alpha-arbutin
summary: Gentler tyrosinase inhibitor for dark spots.
lead: Alpha-arbutin is a synthetic glycosylated hydroquinone, the alpha anomer of the plant compound arbutin (beta-arbutin). It is used in cosmetic serums and creams to lighten dark spots, freckles, melasma and uneven tone, and is marketed as a potentially safer alternative to hydroquinone.

name: Kojic acid
summary: Fungal-derived tyrosinase inhibitor used in brightening products.
lead: Kojic acid is an organic compound, a derivative of 4-pyrone, produced by several fungi, notably Aspergillus oryzae (known in Japan as koji), and formed as a by-product when rice is fermented for sake. It chelates metal ions, including copper and iron, and is used in food to prevent browning and in cosmetics to lighten skin.

name: Cysteamine
summary: Topical depigmenting agent with solid melasma studies.
lead: Cysteamine (2-aminoethanethiol, mercaptamine) is a small organosulfur compound containing both an amine and a thiol group. It is made naturally in mammals during the breakdown of coenzyme A and is used as a medicine for nephropathic cystinosis, a lysosomal storage disease in which cystine accumulates in cells.

name: Salicylic acid
summary: Oil-soluble BHA that gets inside pores and unclogs them.
lead: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid, C7H6O3) is a lipophilic beta hydroxy acid that occurs naturally in willow bark and other plants and is also made industrially. It is a metabolite and chemical precursor of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) and is a plant defense hormone . In dermatology and cosmetics it is used as a keratolytic, meaning an agent that helps the outer layer of skin shed, and it appears in washes, toners, leave-on treatments, medicated pads, wart treatments, dandruff shampoos and chemical peels .
claims: Salicylic acid washes and sprays clear back and chest acne
A salicylic acid astringent helps prevent ingrown hairs after shaving
Salicylic acid is a mild fix that helps with testosterone-induced acne
Salicylic acid washes sometimes worsen or burn skin

name: Glycolic acid
summary: AHA exfoliant for glow, texture, and surface renewal.
lead: Glycolic acid (hydroxyacetic acid, HOCH2COOH) is the smallest alpha hydroxy acid (AHA). It is a colorless, odorless, water-soluble crystalline solid that occurs in sugarcane, sugar beets, pineapple, unripe grapes and other plants, and is also made industrially . In skin care and dermatology it is used as a chemical exfoliant, both in home products at low concentrations and in higher-strength professional peels .
claims: AHAs such as glycolic acid make skin look significantly better
Glycolic acid and retinoids are inexpensive ingredients sold at a large markup
Stronger glycolic acid products give faster results

name: Lactic acid
summary: Gentler AHA that exfoliates and hydrates at once.
lead: Lactic acid (C3H6O3) is an alpha hydroxy acid (AHA) that occurs in sour milk and fermented foods and is produced in animal tissue as lactate during normal metabolism and exercise . In skin care it is used as a keratolytic exfoliant in serums, lotions and professional peels, and Wikipedia notes its use in topical preparations and cosmetics for pH adjustment, disinfectant and keratolytic properties . Salts such as ammonium lactate are used in moisturizers for dry skin .

name: Ceramides
summary: Rebuild the skin barrier and lock in moisture.
lead: Ceramides are a family of waxy lipid molecules, each made of a sphingosine base joined to a fatty acid by an amide bond. They are found in the membranes of eukaryotic cells, take part in cell signaling such as differentiation, proliferation and programmed cell death, and are a component of vernix caseosa, the waxy coating on newborn skin .

name: Urea
summary: Humectant + keratolytic that fixes rough, dry, flaky skin.
lead: Urea (carbamide, CO(NH2)2) is a colorless, odorless, water-soluble compound that is the main nitrogen-containing end product of protein metabolism in mammals, formed in the liver through the urea cycle and excreted in urine. It is practically non-toxic, and most industrial production goes to fertilizer . In 1828 Friedrich Wöhler showed that urea could be made from inorganic starting materials, a milestone in the history of chemistry .

name: Hyaluronic acid
summary: Holds ~1000x its weight in water. Hydration and temporary plumping; injectable forms are fillers.
lead: Hyaluronic acid (HA, hyaluronan) is an anionic, non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan found throughout connective, epithelial and neural tissue. It is unusually large, with human synovial HA averaging around 7 MDa per molecule in one description, and an average 70 kg person holds roughly 15 grams, about a third of which turns over each day . It is a major component of the extracellular matrix, synovial fluid and cartilage .
